## The idea

EEGManySteps is a grassroots initiative in mobile brain/body imaging (MoBI). It is not a classic replication study. Instead, it collects and harmonises walking EEG recorded with many different setups around the world, both existing datasets and new recordings, to find out which acquisition and analysis factors most affect how consistent and reliable gait-related EEG results are.

The community settled on four research goals:

1. step-specific time-frequency patterns,
2. gait-related artefacts across EEG systems,
3. the influence of preprocessing on EEG results during walking, and
4. gait-related modulation of secondary-task correlates such as the P3.

## Harmonised data

Contributed datasets are converted to EEG-BIDS and [Motion-BIDS](../software/index.qmd#bids). They also get EEGManySteps metadata: indoor or outdoor, treadmill or overground, footwear, secondary task, speed scheme and synchronisation method. Sensor locations follow the [UNISEP](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.21159) sensor-placement vocabulary, and gait events are standardised. For new recordings, the project shares a [harmonised auditory oddball paradigm](https://github.com/EEGManySteps/eegmanysteps_oddball) that can be run while standing and while walking.

## My role

I am on the steering committee and co-presented the kick-off meeting in September 2024. I help maintain the website and the [GitHub organisation](https://github.com/EEGManySteps), co-authored the project posters at Methods in Mobile EEG 2025 and Psychologie und Gehirn 2025, and contribute a walking dataset together with Nadine Jacobsen. The project is a natural partner of my work on [reporting standards for mobile EEG](meta-rep.qmd).
